P01-005.boundary_rationale: Onset: 3:12 וַתִּשָּׂאֵ֣נִי ר֔וּחַ (oshb:Ezek.3.12) (“Then the Spirit lifted me up” (web:Ezek.3.12)) begins the return-transport away from the plain-vision back to the exiles, distinct in texture from the preceding commissioning speech (no address, no imperative - narrated action). 3:14 carries the hand-of-YHWH construct, וְיַד יְהוָ֥ה עָלַ֖י חָזָֽקָה (oshb:Ezek.3.14) ('the hand of YHWH was strong upon me'); it is weighed and NOT read as a fresh vision onset here, in contrast to 1:3 and 3:22 - it sits inside a single continuous journey (lifted up → went in bitterness → came to Tel-abib) with no scene change around it, so it is weighed as a licensed rival and held, as the rejected alternative states. Close: 3:15, וָאֵשֵׁ֥ב שָׁ֛ם שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִ֖ים מַשְׁמִ֥ים בְּתוֹכָֽם (oshb:Ezek.3.15) (“I sat there overwhelmed among them seven days” (web:Ezek.3.15)); no parashah mark is recorded at 3:15, which is not read as counterevidence against the seam. The ground this row's boundary evidence rests on is that close with its far face: 3:15 ends the return journey on the seven-day sitting and 3:16 opens on its own strict word-event, while the one licensed rival inside the span, at 3:14, is weighed and held on stated grounds. The gap this close answers is temporal, not formulaic: 3:16 reopens on “At the end of seven days” (web:Ezek.3.16) with its own strict word-event.
P01-005.strongest_rejected_alternative: A cut at 3:13/3:14 is the live rival, weighed here face by face and not taken. Its near face, 3:14, carries two candidate drivers at once: the transport clause וְר֥וּחַ נְשָׂאַ֖תְנִי וַתִּקָּחֵ֑נִי (oshb:Ezek.3.14), which places 3:14, like the onset verse 3:12, among the transport verses the book counts (sweep: 33 verses / 46 occurrences), and the hand-of-YHWH construct, which could be read as a fresh vision onset. Its far face, 3:13, is the sound of the creatures' wings and wheels, with no close-role formula and no parashah mark recorded on it (single-witness). Because a transport verb licenses a seam, the rival is not dismissed; it is held on two stated grounds. A row under three verses is held only for a complete word-event unit, and this cut would leave 3:12-13 and 3:14-15 as rows of two verses each, neither of them such a unit. And no scene change accompanies it: the same journey that begins at 3:12 continues without interruption through 3:15, so treating every occurrence of the construct as onset-grade would read a rival this single journey holds as a hard seam.
P01-005.device_notes: Hand-of-YHWH at 3:14 is one of the book's 7 verses carrying the construct but is weighed here as a licensed rival and held rather than read as a fresh onset (contrast the unit-opening uses at 1:3 and 3:22). K/Q at 3:15 checked before quoting: the unit's own splice above reads the qere form. Paseq at 3:13 disclosed count-only, single-witness.

P01-006.boundary_rationale: Onset: 3:16 carries the book's first strict word-event formula, וַיְהִ֕י מִקְצֵ֖ה שִׁבְעַ֣ת יָמִ֑ים וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Ezek.3.16) (“At the end of seven days, Yahweh’s word came to me, saying” (web:Ezek.3.16)), a hard seam, since a strict word-event opens a new oracle and no unit runs across one (3:16 is one of the 39 strict-form verses and one of the 48 in the first-person family). A pe is recorded after this verse (single-witness); this witness's section marks carry no intra-verse position, so no claim is made about where within or after 3:16 the mark stands, ahead of 3:17's watchman charge, צֹפֶ֥ה נְתַתִּ֖יךָ לְבֵ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל (oshb:Ezek.3.17) (“I have made you a watchman to the house of Israel” (web:Ezek.3.17)). A samekh follows 3:19, between the wicked-man case (3:18-19) and the righteous-man case (3:20-21); disclosed as an internal paragraph mark, not a unit cut, since both cases are one paired illustration of the same watchman charge and no fresh onset device stands at 3:20. Close: 3:21, at the second samekh (single-witness), before the hand-of-YHWH reopens the scene at 3:22. The close's own face is the end of the reader-facing charge and not a counted formula: 3:21 finishes the righteous-man case with no word-event, no messenger formula, no utterance signature and no recognition refrain in the verse, so the samekh recorded on it is the only corroboration the seam carries, and that is the evidence this row's boundary rests on.

P01-010.boundary_rationale: Onset: 6:1 וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Ezek.6.1), “Yahweh’s word came to me, saying” (web:Ezek.6.1), a strict word-event, hard seam. 6:2 opens the oracle's direction with שִׂ֥ים פָּנֶ֖יךָ אֶל הָרֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל (oshb:Ezek.6.2) (“set your face toward the mountains of Israel” (web:Ezek.6.2)). A 2mp recognition-family close occurs mid-unit at 6:7, וִֽידַעְתֶּ֖ם כִּֽי אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה (oshb:Ezek.6.7) ('and you shall know that I am Yahweh'); it is disclosed but read as paragraph-final rather than unit-final, since 6:8 continues without a fresh onset device (“Yet I will leave a remnant” (web:Ezek.6.8)). Close: 6:10, the strict recognition formula וְיָדְע֖וּ כִּֽי אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Ezek.6.10) ('and they shall know that I am Yahweh'), with a pe recorded after it (single-witness), immediately before a fresh messenger formula reopens the address at 6:11. That closing formula is not verse-final: it stands at the head of 6:10 and the verse runs on to the not-in-vain clause, so the close rests on a mid-verse formula with a paragraph mark behind it, and that is the ground this row's boundary evidence records.

P02-019.boundary_rationale: Onset: oshb:Ezek.14.1 וַיָּב֤וֹא אֵלַי֙ אֲנָשִׁ֔ים מִזִּקְנֵ֖י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיֵּשְׁב֖וּ לְפָנָֽי — “Then some of the elders of Israel came to me and sat before me.” (web:Ezek.14.1) — is a bare narrative scene-opener with no formula; a pe follows this very verse (single-witness), and the word-event formula proper opens the next verse, oshb:Ezek.14.2 וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר. Behind the onset, MT 13:23 ends on the second-person feminine-plural recognition refrain (sweep: 64 verses) and carries no mark (single-witness), so this onset has a close-role signal on its far face while its own near face carries no device. The row opens at 14:1 rather than 14:2 because the elders' scene-setting is what the oracle answers (“Should I be inquired of at all by them?” (web:Ezek.14.3)). Close: oshb:Ezek.14.11 לְ֠מַעַן לֹֽא יִתְע֨וּ ע֤וֹד בֵּֽית יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ מֵאַֽחֲרַ֔י וְלֹֽא יִטַּמְּא֥וּ ע֖וֹד בְּכָל פִּשְׁעֵיהֶ֑ם וְהָ֥יוּ לִ֣י לְעָ֗ם וַֽאֲנִי֙ אֶהְיֶ֤ה לָהֶם֙ לֵֽאלֹהִ֔ים נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה ends with the utterance formula נאם אדני יהוה; a second pe follows this verse (single-witness), so this witness records a pe on both the first and the last verse of the row, and only the second of them stands at a seam. Both sides: the close is formula-plus-pe (single-witness), while the onset rests on the elders' scene alone, because the pe recorded on 14:1 (single-witness) falls inside the row, parting 14:1 from 14:2, and so speaks for the rival weighed below rather than for this onset.
P02-019.strongest_rejected_alternative: Opening the row at 14:2, the word-event proper, rather than at 14:1 is the rival that matters, and it is weighed below. On the rival's own side of the seam the evidence is strong: oshb:Ezek.14.2 carries the strict word-event formula, one of that formula's 39 verses. Behind it stands the elders' scene at oshb:Ezek.14.1, which carries no formula of its own. The parashah layer speaks for the RIVAL and not for this row, and it is written up that way: MEASURED in this witness, a pe is recorded on MT 14:1 (single-witness), and the witness keys a break to the verse it follows, so it parts 14:1 from 14:2 — exactly where the rival would cut. Since no mark licenses a seam on its own, the corroboration is disclosed and left unadopted. The row opens at 14:1 all the same, on two stated grounds. First, the elders' scene at 14:1 is the setting the oracle answers, and it comes before the word-event at 14:2, so the row opens at 14:1. Second, a row under three verses is held only for a complete word-event unit, and the one-verse row at 14:1 that the rival's cut would leave behind is no such unit. Holding a licensed rival on stated grounds is what this row's boundary evidence amounts to: the onset turns on a scene change at 14:1 that carries no device of its own, and the licensed word-event at 14:2 is weighed and held on the two grounds just stated.
P02-019.device_notes: K/Q at oshb:Ezek.14.4 is disclosed above; paseq at 14.4 and 14.6 is count-only, single-witness. Four marks fall inside the span, each single-witness: the pe on MT 14:1, weighed in the rejected alternative, and three mid-row samekh marks at oshb:Ezek.14.3, oshb:Ezek.14.5 and oshb:Ezek.14.8 (disclosed as internal corroboration of the paragraph structure, not read as competing seams); no parashah mark falls at oshb:Ezek.14.4. The samekh on 14:8 stands after a refrain-grade close: that verse ends on the 2mp recognition refrain וִֽידַעְתֶּ֖ם כִּֽי אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה (oshb:Ezek.14.8), a member of the counted 2mp form (sweep: 21 verses) and of the wider recognition family (sweep: 64 verses), and the same verse makes the man a sign and a byword, לְא֣וֹת וְלִמְשָׁלִ֔ים (oshb:Ezek.14.8). That close is disclosed and argues no cut, because no fresh onset device stands between it and the utterance signature that closes the row at 14:11. This 11-verse row is over the 7-10 verse target; disclosed as over the target, not over a cap.

P03-001.device_notes: Whole-chapter span disclosed as the row's own density: the chapter is 8 verses and is kept as one row rather than split at its internal samekh (15:5, single witness). This span carries no K/Q note, no paseq, and the editorial-note layer is silent across it. A pe is written after MT 14:23 (single witness), the front-seam break behind a chapter whose own riddle starts at 15:1. Inside the application, 15:6-8, MT 15:7 carries the second-person plural recognition clause, counted among the 2mp recognition verses (sweep: 21 verses) and within the wider recognition family (sweep: 64 verses), followed in that verse only by a dependent infinitive clause on setting the face against them, so in effect it closes the application's verdict; it is disclosed as a refrain-grade close inside the row and argues no cut, since only the chapter's final verse, with its utterance signature, stands after it.
P03-001.boundary_rationale: Onset side: MT 15:1 opens with the strict word-event formula, וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Ezek.15.1), immediately followed by the address בֶּן אָדָ֕ם (oshb:Ezek.15.2) at 15:2, which puts the riddle about the useless vine-wood in the standard oracle-onset frame. Close side: the row's final verse, MT 15:8, ends the applied sentence against Jerusalem's inhabitants and carries the utterance-of-the-Lord-YHWH signature at its own end, matched by a pe mark recorded on 15:8 in the single-witness paragraph layer. A samekh mark sits earlier, on 15:5 (sweep: 8 verses), where the riddle's own question -- whether the vine-wood, even charred, is fit for any use -- reaches its rhetorical dead end before the messenger formula כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה (oshb:Ezek.15.6) opens the application at 15:6. That mid-chapter mark is weighed and not adopted as the row seam: the application (15:6-8) answers the riddle (15:1-5) rather than opening an independent formula-bounded unit of its own, and a three-verse application row would not itself carry a fresh word-event onset. The row is therefore kept as the whole chapter, with the internal mark disclosed rather than acted on. Both outer faces carry a formula and a mark together, and what holds this row's boundary evidence where it stands is the reading just disclosed: the samekh on 15:5 (single-witness) leaves the riddle-to-application seam inside the row weighed and unadopted, an internal question this record states rather than settles.

P03-004.boundary_rationale: Onset side: MT 16:20 opens a sharper escalation with no fresh formula device, וַתִּקְחִ֞י אֶת בָּנַ֤יִךְ וְאֶת בְּנוֹתַ֨יִךְ֙ (oshb:Ezek.16.20) (the WEB has “you have taken your sons and your daughters”, web:Ezek.16.20), continuing the same word-event unit by default. Close side: MT 16:23 closes the row, and its final clause is the double cry and utterance formula א֣וֹי א֣וֹי לָ֔ךְ נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה (oshb:Ezek.16.23) ('woe, woe to you, declares the Lord YHWH'), a verse-final close reached after the summary at 16:22 recalls the days of the addressee's youth. No parashah mark falls in this four-verse stretch (sweep: 4 verses); the seam again rests on the verse-final formula alone. The onset's own evidence is that content turn alone, with no formula device standing at 16:20, while the close carries a verse-final woe-cry with the utterance signature after it; that asymmetry between the two faces is what this row's boundary evidence records. Two single Ketiv/Qere notes fall inside this span: MT 16:20 reads (oshb:Ezek.16.20) the ketiv מתזנתך and MT 16:22 reads (oshb:Ezek.16.22) the ketiv זכרתי.
P03-004.device_notes: Two single Ketiv/Qere notes disclosed above (16:20, 16:22). No paseq, no editorial note and no parashah mark fall inside this span. The and-you-took anaphora runs across this row's onset seam: the same verb opens 16:16, 16:17, 16:18 and 16:20 (oshb:Ezek.16.16, oshb:Ezek.16.17, oshb:Ezek.16.18, oshb:Ezek.16.20), disclosed here as a continuity signal weighed against an onset that rests on the content turn alone. 16:23's temporal frame is completed only by 16:24 (oshb:Ezek.16.24), one sentence running across the close seam: a second continuity signal, weighed and not taken as decisive against the verse-final woe-cry and utterance signature.

P03-013.strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading 17:22-24 as a separate restoration oracle, on the same footing as the covenant turn at 16:59-63, was weighed and not taken: 17:22-24 keeps the tree figure the riddle sets up at 17:3 and opens on the same messenger formula that carries the interpretation from 17:11 onward, rather than turning to covenant language as 16:59 does, so no category deviation is disclosed here.

P04-013.boundary_rationale: Onset: MT 21:6 (= WEB 21:1) carries the word-event formula, וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר (web:Ezek.21.1 = oshb:Ezek.21.6), and its far face, MT 21:5 (= WEB 20:49), ends on the prophet's own outcry, וָאֹמַ֕ר אֲהָ֖הּ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה (web:Ezek.20.49 = oshb:Ezek.21.5), which is no close-role formula; a pe is recorded on that far verse (single-witness), the mark standing after the verse it follows and so at this onset seam, which leaves the onset licensed on its near face alone. Close: MT 21:12 (= WEB 21:7) ends verse-final on the utterance signature, נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה (web:Ezek.21.7 = oshb:Ezek.21.12), with a pe recorded on that same verse (single-witness), and its far face, MT 21:13 (= WEB 21:8), opens a fresh word-event formula, so both faces of the close are signalled. Interior: the recognition at the head of MT 21:10 (= WEB 21:5), וְיָֽדְעוּ֙ כָּל בָּשָׂ֔ר (web:Ezek.21.5 = oshb:Ezek.21.10), runs on into two further clauses and so stands mid-verse, and a samekh is recorded on MT 21:10 (single-witness), parting it from the verse after it; MT 21:11 (= WEB 21:6) then opens the groaning with וְאַתָּ֥ה בֶן אָדָ֖ם (web:Ezek.21.6 = oshb:Ezek.21.11) and no change of addressee - an onset-class device this cut does not license, weighed in the rejected alternative and held as paragraph-grade.
P04-013.strongest_rejected_alternative: The rival that matters inside this span is a cut between MT 21:10 and MT 21:11 (= WEB 21:5/21:6), and it is weighed face by face. Its near face, MT 21:11, turns the spoken sword oracle into an enacted groaning on an and-you address to the prophet, an onset-class device; its far face, MT 21:10, carries the recognition formula with the all-flesh subject infixed, which leaves that formula mid-verse rather than verse-final, and the samekh recorded on MT 21:10 (single-witness) corroborates the same seam. The cut is not taken: the addressee does not change across it, the groaning interprets the drawn sword just announced instead of opening a fresh oracle, and a paragraph mark standing behind a mid-verse formula is paragraph-grade evidence rather than a seam. A second reading, that the two groaning verses stand as a unit of their own, is weighed and declined here too: a row of two verses is held only for a complete word-event unit, and MT 21:11-21:12 carries no word-event of its own.
P04-013.device_notes: This witness records a mark on the verse it follows. Inside this span a samekh stands on MT 21:10 (= WEB 21:5), single-witness, parting the mid-verse recognition from the groaning that follows, and a pe stands on MT 21:12 (= WEB 21:7), single-witness, at this row's close; behind the onset a pe stands on MT 21:5 (= WEB 20:49), single-witness. One paseq is recorded within MT 21:8 (= WEB 21:3), count-only and single-witness, with no position inside the verse claimed. Category note, in one sentence: the groaning at MT 21:11-21:12 (= WEB 21:6-21:7) is an enacted sign standing inside the spoken sword oracle, and although this book's own sectioning reads those two verses as a sign-act unit of their own, a row of two verses is held only for a complete word-event unit, so they are kept here and disclosed rather than cut out.

P05-007.boundary_rationale: Onset: 24:1 is a HARD SEAM — the siege dateline, the 5th of the 14 oracle datelines in canonical order (1:1, 1:2, 8:1, 20:1, 24:1, 26:1, 29:1, 29:17, 30:20, 31:1, 32:1, 32:17, 33:21, 40:1) — and simultaneously the word-event formula with the date infixed between the word for "to me" and the word for "saying": present in the 41-verse vayehi-any word-event count and ABSENT from the strict 39-verse count (the infix breaks the adjacency the strict form requires). Whole verse = "וַיְהִי֩ דְבַר יְהוָ֨ה אֵלַ֜י בַּשָּׁנָ֤ה הַתְּשִׁיעִית֙ בַּחֹ֣דֶשׁ הָעֲשִׂירִ֔י בֶּעָשׂ֥וֹר לַחֹ֖דֶשׁ לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Ezek.24.1)". Close: 24:14 stacks TWO close-grade formulae on one verse — the emphatic "I, YHWH, have spoken" (sweep: 14 verses) and the utterance formula (sweep: 81 verses) — whole verse = "אֲנִ֨י יְהוָ֤ה דִּבַּ֨רְתִּי֙ בָּאָ֣ה וְעָשִׂ֔יתִי לֹֽא אֶפְרַ֥ע וְלֹא אָח֖וּס וְלֹ֣א אֶנָּחֵ֑ם כִּדְרָכַ֤יִךְ וְכַעֲלִילוֹתַ֨יִךְ֙ שְׁפָט֔וּךְ נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהֹוִֽה (oshb:Ezek.24.14)".
P05-007.strongest_rejected_alternative: Two alternatives were weighed for MT 24:1, and a third inside the row. (1) Treating 24:1-27 as ONE unit (24:1 as the head of this collection's entire last movement, no further internal cut) — rejected because 24:15 carries its own full-form strict word-event onset (a hard seam in its own right) and a genre shift from mashal to sign-act, and both halves carry independent formula closes (24:14 and 24:27); collapsing them would also make one row far longer than the 7-10 verse target length. (2) Treating 24:1 as its OWN one-verse dated complex, separate from 24:2-14 — rejected because a dateline fused with a word-event in one verse is treated as a single onset that never splits, and because the day-naming command stands at 24:2, “write the name of the day, this same day” (web:Ezek.24.2), with the mashal's own opening command following at 24:3 (verse-final words "שְׁפֹ֔ת וְגַם יְצֹ֥ק בּ֖וֹ מָֽיִם (oshb:Ezek.24.3)"), so the parable runs straight on from the date with no seam between them. (3) Cutting at 24:8/24:9 - the alternative the Masoretic paragraph layer proposes, named and weighed here. What the rival's near face carries: MEASURED from the pointed Hebrew witness, MT 24:9 opens on the long-form messenger formula after a therefore-particle (oshb:Ezek.24.9). What its far face carries: MEASURED, the witness records a PE (petuchah, open section, single-witness) after MT 24:8 - and nothing else, because MEASURED from the pointed Hebrew witness MT 24:8 ends on a purpose infinitive (oshb:Ezek.24.8), with no utterance, recognition or I-YHWH-have-spoken signature anywhere in that verse. Whether it is licensed: it is NOT, since a messenger formula cuts only through a change of addressee or a close-role formula ending the verse before it. The first fails, because the addressee does not change - MT 24:6 already addresses the bloody city (oshb:Ezek.24.6) and MT 24:9 addresses that same city. The second fails, because the verse immediately before it does not END on a close-role formula, and a mark alone never supplies one. The stated ground on which this row holds: a section mark ranks below any licensed text signal, so the PE after MT 24:8 is weak corroboration, disclosed FOR the alternative it corroborates and not for this row, and it is outranked by the licensed drivers this row does rest on - the fused dateline-plus-word-event onset at 24:1 and the stacked I-YHWH-have-spoken plus utterance close at 24:14. So the 24:8/24:9 cut is an unlicensed, one-faced rival: weighed, disclosed and held, its near face carrying a messenger formula that neither an addressee change nor a close-role formula behind it licenses, and its far face carrying no close-role formula at all.

In the WEB, “The Lord Yahweh says to Tyre: ‘Won’t the islands shake at the sound of your fall, when the wounded groan, when the slaughter is made within you?” (web:Ezek.26.15). 26:17 embeds the noun "וְנָשְׂא֨וּ עָלַ֤יִךְ קִינָה֙ וְאָ֣מְרוּ לָ֔ךְ אֵ֣יךְ אָבַ֔דְתְּ נוֹשֶׁ֖בֶת מִיַּמִּ֑ים הָעִ֣יר הַהֻלָּ֗לָה אֲשֶׁר֩ הָיְתָ֨ה חֲזָקָ֤ה בַיָּם֙ הִ֣יא וְיֹשְׁבֶ֔יהָ אֲשֶׁר נָתְנ֥וּ חִתִּיתָ֖ם לְכָל יוֹשְׁבֶֽיהָ" (oshb:Ezek.26.17), "lamentation/qinah" — but as REPORTED future speech the sea-princes will voice ("they shall take up a qinah over you"), not a command to the prophet; disclosed here as texture, not treated as a lament_qinah onset. 26:18 ends "עַתָּה֙ יֶחְרְד֣וּ הָֽאִיִּ֔ן י֖וֹם מַפַּלְתֵּ֑ךְ וְנִבְהֲל֛וּ הָאִיִּ֥ים אֲשֶׁר בַּיָּ֖ם מִצֵּאתֵֽךְ" (oshb:Ezek.26.18) with NO recognition, utterance, or "I YHWH have spoken" formula in the verse; a SAMEKH follows immediately (single-witness), disclosed as paragraph texture rather than a row-final close, because 26:19 reopens the same messenger formula ("כִּ֣י כֹ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה…", oshb:Ezek.26.19) against the SAME 2fs addressee (Tyre), so no addressee-class shift separates 26:15-18 from 26:19-21 and the mark alone does not license a cut here; that seam is disclosed as paragraph-grade. 'Son of man' at Ezek.36.17 בֶּן אָדָ֗ם בֵּ֤ית יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ יֹשְׁבִ֣ים עַל אַדְמָתָ֔ם וַיְטַמְּא֣וּ אוֹתָ֔הּ בְּדַרְכָּ֖ם וּבַעֲלִֽילוֹתָ֑ם כְּטֻמְאַת֙ הַנִּדָּ֔ה הָיְתָ֥ה דַרְכָּ֖ם לְפָנָֽי (oshb:Ezek.36.17) opens a retrospective on Israel's own defilement of the land and the resulting exile — a distinct tense and topic from the 'mountains of Israel' address just closed. P11-010.boundary_rationale: Onset: a transport verb at Ezek.47.1 (“He brought me back to the door of the temple” (web:Ezek.47.1)) continues the vision after the hard seam at 46.24/47.1; a second transport verb follows immediately at 47.2, then the measuring sequence proper (3-5, four successive measured wadings) -- disclosed as a one-sentence category deviation from a pure vision narrative, since the passage briefly carries the measurement lists' own device before returning to vision narrative. The row covers the river's rise from the threshold (1-2), the four measured wadings (3-5), the 'have you seen, son of man' address (6) and the return to the bank, the riverside trees and the healed sea (7-10), the unhealed swamps (11, a K/Q verse), and the closing description of the riverbank trees bearing monthly fruit (12), where the construction glossed 'its months' is disclosed as the book's final chodesh-root homograph, not a date formula. Close: 47.12 ends on a descriptive clause about the riverbank trees, with no close formula in the verse; the samekh recorded on Ezek.47.12 (single-witness) corroborates that close, and the next verse, 47.13, opens with a fresh messenger formula addressed to the land-division topic -- a genre shift from vision to statute, the hard seam at 47.12/47.13. The close's own face is therefore content rather than formula, and that is the ground this row's boundary evidence records.
P11-010.strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting at 47.5/47.6 to isolate the measuring circuit (47.3-5) as its own temple_measurement row. It is weighed and held on stated grounds. The rival's near face, Ezek.47.6, IS licensed: the verse is both a said-to-me verse and a guided-motion verse (וַיּוֹלִכֵ֥נִי, וַיְשִׁבֵ֖נִי), and it is a transport verse of the counted class (sweep: 33 verses), so a seam there would not be device-free. Its far face, Ezek.47.5, carries the fourth measure-verb occurrence and a content close (נַ֖חַל אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא יֵעָבֵֽר), with no close-role formula and no parashah mark, so the rival is one-faced rather than two-faced. The row holds against it on three stated grounds: Ezek.47.6's question looks BACK at the measuring just reported and its motion returns the prophet to the bank inside one scene rather than opening a new one; the river vision runs 47:1-12 as one measured circuit with 47:6 inside it as interior texture; and the only further signal at 47:6 is the English version's mid-verse paragraph break, a translator's layout choice that corroborates no seam. Guided-motion verbs stand inside the measuring circuit, though not at its head: MEASURED over the pointed Hebrew witness, Ezek.47.3 does not BEGIN with a guided-motion verb (it opens בְּצֵאת הָאִ֥ישׁ) but does carry וַיַּעֲבִרֵ֥נִי later in the verse, and Ezek.47.4 carries that same form twice. Both verses are members of the same counted class, standing inside the measuring circuit, weighed and not taken, since each of those verbs steps the prophet one wading further after a measuring of a thousand cubits rather than opening a new scene. The measuring sequence therefore remains texture inside the single river vision running 47.1-12, disclosed as a one-sentence category deviation rather than split into a separate row (oshb:Ezek.47.5, oshb:Ezek.47.3, oshb:Ezek.47.6).
P11-010.device_notes: Category deviation, disclosed: this row's span briefly carries temple_measurement's own device (the four measured wadings, 47.3-5) inside an otherwise plain vision narrative; disclosed in this one sentence rather than split into a separate row, since no formula bounds 47.3-5 off on either side. The two transport verses inside that circuit were weighed as rival onsets and not taken. A seam at 47.2/47.3 would strand 47.1-2 as a two-verse row, and a row that short is held only for a complete word-event unit, which those two verses are not; a seam at 47.3/47.4 would part the second measuring of a thousand from the one before it. Neither far face carries a close formula or a mark (single-witness), 47.2 ending on water trickling from the right-hand side and 47.3 on ankle-deep water, and in neither candidate does the guided-motion form open the verse, 47.3 opening on the man's going out and 47.4 on the measure verb, so both rivals are one-faced and weaker than the 47.5/47.6 rival. K/Q notes fall at Ezek.47.8, 47.10, 47.11 and 47.12 inside this row -- a locally dense cluster -- disclosed as textual-variant sites; no boundary is argued from any of them. Ezek.47.12 carries the construction glossed 'its months', the last of the book's chodesh-root homographs, disclosed as NOT a date formula. The speech to the prophet at 47.8 is a licensed onset wherever it stands inside a vision; it is weighed as a rival at 47.7/47.8 and held, since it interprets the river just measured inside one scene, while 47.7 ends on the riverside trees with no close-role formula and no mark (single-witness). P11-013.boundary_rationale: Onset: no formula device opens Ezek.48.30 (“These are the exits of the city” (web:Ezek.48.30)); what stands behind it at 48.29/48.30 is the Ezek.48.29 close, an utterance signature with a pe recorded on that verse (single-witness), together with the topic shift from the tribal-portion summary to the city gates. The row covers the city's four sides, their measurements and named gates (30-34), and the book's final verse (35), the city's circumference and its new name. Close: the book's own end. No formula closes 48.35; no parashah mark is recorded after it, since none is possible on the book's last verse; a paseq is recorded within it (count-only, single-witness). This is disclosed as the row's own close condition rather than argued as a gap or omission.

P11-015.boundary_rationale: Onset: Ezek.48.23 reopens the tribal-portion list on its own explicit resumption formula, the vav-initial “the rest of the tribes” (web:Ezek.48.23), a change of listed object back from the holy portion, city and prince's land to the remaining southern tribes -- behind it, 48.22 closes the prince's portion with no formula and no mark (single-witness), so the resumption at 48.23 stands as the onset's own evidence. The row covers the five southern tribal portions in the same 'one portion' refrain as the northern block, Benjamin through Gad (23-27), each closing on its own 'one portion' formula; no cut falls inside this refrain block. Verses 28-29 close the whole allotment: 48.28 gives Gad's own southern border to the Mediterranean, and 48.29 summarises the entire land division with the utterance signature and the pe parashah mark on the same verse -- a doubled close signal matching the samekh-plus-utterance doubled close already recorded at 47.23 (samekh there; pe here, disclosed distinctly). Close: the pe recorded after Ezek.48.29 ends the row; the next verse, 48.30, turns to the city's gates on a fresh, distinct topic.

The onset's ground is that list resumption at 48.23, “the rest of the tribes” (web:Ezek.48.23), which carries no onset device of its own, set against 48.22's close of the prince's portion with no formula and no mark (single-witness).
